newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says no decision on higher dividend.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says no decision on higher dividend.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp has not decided whether to raise its annual dividend in the 1996/97 business year ending March, a Toyota spokesman said on Monday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun economic daily reported on Sunday that Toyota is likely to raise its annual dividend by one to two yen from the 19 yen it paid in 1995/96. This would be the first increase in eight years, it said.
"The Nikkei's story is speculation. We have not decided about dividend payments in 1996/97," a Toyota spokesman said.
Toyota's payout ratio stood at 39 percent in 1995/96, 48.9 percent in the nine months to March 1995 and 63.9 percent in the year to June 1994, the spokesman said.
If Toyota does raise the annual dividend to 19 yen in 1996/97, the payout ratio will fall to 27 percent in view of an estimated parent net profit of 260 billion yen that year.

"Honda is sure to raise its dividend by one yen this year (from the 14 yen paid in 1995/96), but Toyota may use its extra profits to buy back shares rather than increase the dividend," Kankaku Research senior analyst Nobuaki Yanachi said.
Stock buy-backs help investors by reducing the number of outstanding shares, which improves a company's return on equity and thus makes its shares more attractive to new investors.
Toyota's share price stood at 2,690 yen at 0344 GMT, steady from Friday's close, while Honda Motor Co Ltd rose 20 yen from Friday to 2,700 yen.
